newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom said to keep exclusive rights.
newsitem.headline: Telkom said to keep exclusive rights.

text.p: State-run telecommunications giant PT Telkom would keep its exclusive rights to provide long-distance and domestic phones calls until 2006 and 2011 respectively, the Jakarta Post reported on Tuesday.

Jonathan L. Parapak, secretary-general of the tourism, post and telecommunications ministry, was quoted as saying Telkom's rights would not be changed, even though private firms had shown interest in providing domestic telecommunications services.
"They are allowed to express interests only but the regulations will not change," Parapak was quoted as saying.
Telkom share prices had been hit in the past week following news on the possible emergence of a competitor providing basic telecommunications services, brokers said.
Speculation has been that the potential competitors included companies owned by Bambang Trihatmodjo, the second son of President Suharto, and Sudwikatmono, a relative of Suharto.
In 1995 the government granted an exclusive right to state-owned PT Indonesia Satellite (Indosat) and privately owned PT Satelindo to run international telecommunications services until year 2005.
Telkom was granted a 10-year monopoly on long-distance calls within Indonesia in 1995. -- Jakarta newsroom 6221 384-6364
